logs.speaker: CREWMAN P. ODUYA
logs.text: Half of night shift sleeps in the tram cars now. Nobody wants to go back to their bunks after Miller. The bulkheads sealed at shift change, and the Super says the lockdown won't take an override from up here. If a tram ever comes back up the spine, I'm on it. I don't care where it goes.

logs.header: AUDIO LOG // CORWIN SABLE, GORGON LIAISON
logs.speaker: CORWIN SABLE, GORGON LIAISON
logs.text: Memo to Gorgon Consolidated, Asset Division. Habitation reports continued tenant attrition in Blocks A and B. In all correspondence, residents are to be described as occupants, not crew. Occupancy will stabilize on its own. I recommend the lockdown remain in force until the recovery team arrives.

logs.speaker: COOK R. DELACROIX
logs.text: I moved what was left of the galley stock up to the Commissary. Families keep coming in for bread. Nobody pays, and I stopped asking. The ones who stand at the windows don't come in anymore. There's a cot behind the bar. If you need somewhere to hide, push on the back wall.

logs.speaker: CHAPLAIN A. MENSAH
logs.text: The last down-line tram left at oh six hundred, before the lockdown. I put every child I could find on it, and as many parents as it would hold. The Sergeant's people counted heads. Whatever is waiting down the spine, it cannot be worse than what hums in these vents at night. I stayed. Someone has to keep the candles lit.

logs.speaker: RESIDENT R. CASTELLANOS
logs.text: Day five. We're in A-3 with the door taped shut. The kids think it's a game. Somebody tries the door code every night, very slowly, one digit at a time. Only family knows the code. My husband went to Hydroponics on day three, and he never came home.

logs.speaker: RESIDENT R. CASTELLANOS
logs.text: I got them on the chaplain's tram. Both of them. There wasn't room for me, and I told them that was fine, and I smiled the whole time. I watched it go down the spine. I'm in A-7 now, because A-3 isn't safe. Somebody keeps saying my name through the vent.

logs.speaker: RESIDENT R. CASTELLANOS
logs.text: Nap time count: nineteen. All nineteen walked to the chapel holding the rope, the way we practice it. Chaplain Mensah says there's a tram. I'm leaving the mats out. When they come back, they'll want their mats.

logs.speaker: CREWMAN P. ODUYA
logs.text: I kept the Friday double feature going for anyone who wanted two hours of not thinking about it. Forty people last week. Tonight, nine. One of the nine didn't get up when the lights came on. He's still sitting in the third row. He hasn't blinked.

logs.speaker: RESIDENT E. NOVAK
logs.text: The lower level of Block B is flooding. The Super said a main burst under the laundry and he'd have it fixed by morning. Then he stopped answering the intercom. The water is warm. Something moves around down there, and there are no fish on this ship.

logs.speaker: RESIDENT E. NOVAK
logs.text: There's current in the water now. The lights down there spark when it moves. The Super is still in the boiler room. I can hear his floor buffer all night, back and forth, back and forth. Nobody's cleaning anything.

logs.speaker: RESIDENT E. NOVAK
logs.text: Rec center log. The pool is closed. Three people went in after the lockdown because they said the water was the only place it was quiet. They're still floating in the deep end. I'm not getting them out. Not after what the first one did when I tried.

logs.speaker: CREWMAN P. ODUYA
logs.text: I'm hiding in the laundry. The machines are loud enough to cover my breathing. Miller came through an hour ago. He walked right past the washers, then stopped and hummed something. The same tune everybody hears. He knew exactly where I was. He just didn't want me yet.

logs.speaker: SUPERINTENDENT G. HOLLIS
logs.text: Maintenance log. A main burst under Block B, and the lower level is flooding. I can flush it from the boiler room, but the lockdown has the valve. The Gorgon man came by and told me to leave it. Said the water keeps them in. I've got a master key and thirty years on this boat. I'm going down there to open it anyway.

logs.header: AUDIO LOG // CORWIN SABLE, GORGON LIAISON
logs.speaker: CORWIN SABLE, GORGON LIAISON
logs.text: Instruction to the Superintendent, copied to Security. The Block B flood is not to be drained. Water is an effective barrier, and it costs nothing. The chaplain's unauthorized tram will be noted in her file. All remaining occupants will stay in their units until collection.

logs.speaker: COOK R. DELACROIX
logs.text: I brought the Super coffee. He's been down here two days with that buffer rig, fighting the valve. He doesn't drink it. He doesn't look up. The rig has grown into his arms. He keeps saying the floor has to be clean before they come. Who's coming, Hollis? Who's coming?
